question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y=2{X}_{1}-3{X}_{2} & ∼N(2{\mu }_{1}-3{\mu }_{2},4{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+9{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(4-3,28+36) \\  & ∼N(1,64).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =1$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{64}=8.$ 

We want to find $P(-4.6<Y<3.48).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-4.6<Y<3.48) & =P(\frac{-4.6-1}{8}<Z<\frac{3.48-1}{8}) \\  & =P(-0.70<Z<0.31) \\  & =P(Z<0.31)-P(Z<-0.70) \\  & =Φ(0.31)-Φ(-0.70)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.31) & ≈0.6217 \\ Φ(-0.70) & ≈0.2420.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-4.6<Y<3.48) & ≈Φ(0.31)-Φ(-0.70) \\  & ≈0.6217-0.2420 \\  & ≈0.3797.\end{aligned}
$$
